rows.title: Platform `mobile` brief: Dragonfly apps
rows.summary: A Dragonfly app has only `.nuc` files and `assets/`; the app is generated in `build/app` (never edit it).
body: A Dragonfly app has only `.nuc` files and `assets/`; the app is generated in `build/app` (never edit it). You write
the business logic; the framework writes the rest (DI, routing, JSON, states, tests). The views use the UI toolkit's
classes from the type definitions (`Text`, `Scaffold`, `Icons.add`), with `name = value` arguments.

rows.title: The `mobile` platform of Dragonfly — Generators
rows.summary: `dragonfly gen resource <component> <Name>` writes the finished, compiling code of a resource (ADR-0103): its models (nested objects become models named `<Name><Key>`; a paged answer gives `<Name>Page`), the repository (an HTTP repository over the app's `Http` connection, a named one added when…
body: `dragonfly gen resource <component> <Name>` writes the finished, compiling code of a resource (ADR-0103): its models

(nested objects become models named `<Name><Key>`; a paged answer gives `<Name>Page`), the repository (an HTTP repository over the app's `Http` connection, a named one added when the app has another), one use

case per action (`--actions list,get,search,create,update,delete`), their aliases in the facade, with `--screen <screen>` a screen that lists it with its state manager and state model, and a test with the repository mocked. The fields
come from an example answer (`--from-json <file|url>`), a spec (`--from-spec <spec.md>`: its example answer, else its
`Key | Type` table; a `GET https://...` line gives the API) or `--fields "id:int name:string"`. A file that exists is
never overwritten (the facade and the repository get only the members they lack, so an action added to a resource that exists is finished); a name another file declares stops it before it writes.
`dragonfly gen inspect` answers what the project has. The agent writes only what is not standard: a use case with
its own rules, a view's details.

rows.title: The `mobile` platform of Dragonfly — Generators
rows.summary: `dragonfly gen usecase <component> <Name>` adds the alias of a use case the project declares to its component's facade; with `--calls <Repository>.<method>` it writes the use case too, when all it does is call that method of a repository.
body: `dragonfly gen usecase <component> <Name>` adds the alias of a use case the project declares to its component's
facade; with `--calls <Repository>.<method>` it writes the use case too, when all it does is call that method of a
repository. What a screen shows of it (a state manager's method and its state) is written by hand.

dragonfly gen usecase characters CharacterEpisodes --calls CharacterRepository.episodes   # a method the repository declares

rows.title: The `mobile` platform of Dragonfly — 3. Rules
rows.summary: 1. Golden rule: performance, speed and readability of the syntax.
body: 1. **Golden rule:** performance, speed and readability of the syntax.
2. **Only the business logic in Nuclear.** Constructors, overrides, registration in the injector, JSON
serialization, http calls, state handling and imports are written by the transpiler.
3. **Light clean architecture:** data, domain and presentation layers, plus what is shared. The layers exist in the
generated code; in Nuclear you do not write interfaces nor classes that only pass data around.
4. **Closed components:** a business component is used from another only through its `appcomponent` (facade). The
5. **The platform's runtime and the official ecosystem of the dialect:** what the UI toolkit lacks (http connections
with cache and retries, session, events, network, ACL, the local database) comes from the dialect's runtime package; the rest from the
6. **The local database is the backend's ORM on the device** (ADR-0096): a model with `@primary` (`@primary(generated = true)`,
`@created`, `@updated` as in a backend entity; `@entity("table")` names the table) has a table, encrypted unless the
project's or the component's config says otherwise (`local: LocalDatabase = LocalDatabase(encrypted = false)`),

rows.title: The `mobile` platform of Dragonfly — 4. Architecture
body: | A `usecase` is only used from an `appcomponent` | `N0301` |
| A `service` is only used from a `usecase` or an `aggregate` | `N0301` |
| An `aggregate` is only used from a `usecase` | `N0301` |
| A `repository` is only used from a `usecase` or an `aggregate` | `N0301` |

| From another component (or from `shared/`, `config/` and `main.nuc`) only the `appcomponent`, the models (`model`), the converters (`converter`), the events (`event`), the global components (`component`), the guards (`guard`) and the screens (`@screen`) are visible | `N0302` |
| The UI toolkit's context and router belong to the views: only a `stateless` or a `stateful` uses them (the names: [flutter.md](flutter.md) §4) | `N0301` |

rows.title: The `mobile` platform of Dragonfly
body: > Inherits every rule of [nuclear-base.md](https://github.com/nuclearlang/nuclear/blob/main/spec/nuclear-base.md) and the standard library ([library.md](https://github.com/nuclearlang/nuclear/blob/main/spec/library.md)).
> This document defines the mobile platform (ADR-0093): apps for Android, iOS, desktop and web through one UI
> toolkit, written in Nuclear only. Today its only dialect is `flutter` ([flutter.md](flutter.md)), whose spec
> holds both the platform's rules and how Flutter writes them; this document is the platform's index. A project's
> Nuclear never changes between the dialects of the platform; only a use of a dialect's type definitions (a
> Flutter widget, a pub.dev package) ties code to that dialect.
